title: A reproducible analysis template I actually use
text: Most analysis projects rot because nobody can re-run them six months later. Here’s the skeleton I start every project with so that make all reproduces everything from raw data to the figures in the paper.

title: A reproducible analysis template I actually use
text:
The layout
project/
├── data/
│   ├── raw/          # never edited by hand
│   └── derived/      # everything here is regenerated
├── R/                # functions, sourced not run top-to-bottom
├── analysis/         # numbered scripts: 01_clean.R, 02_model.R ...
├── figures/
├── renv.lock         # pinned R dependencies
├── Makefile
└── README.md

title: A reproducible analysis template I actually use
section: The rule that makes it work
text:
The rule that makes it work
Raw data is read-only. Everything in data/derived/ is produced by a script and can be deleted and rebuilt at any time. If you can’t delete it and get it back, it doesn’t belong there.

title: A reproducible analysis template I actually use
text:
A tiny Makefile
all: figures/fig1.png

data/derived/clean.rds: analysis/01_clean.R data/raw/source.csv
    Rscript $<

figures/fig1.png: analysis/02_model.R data/derived/clean.rds
    Rscript $<
Make only re-runs what changed. Touch the cleaning script and just the downstream steps rebuild.

title: About
text:
I’m a doctoral researcher in Heidelberg working on climate–health epidemiology and spatial statistics. My methods sit mostly in Bayesian spatiotemporal modeling — R-INLA, BYM2, CAR priors — alongside causal inference (Mendelian randomization) and NLP on geotagged data.
Before this I trained as a dentist and earned master’s degrees in public health/epidemiology and in health informatics. I’ve published 32+ papers (10,000+ citations), including work in The Lancet Planetary Health and two first-author papers in iScience (Cell Press). These days I split my attention between academic research and real-world evidence / HEOR.
